rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the opponents could match the Qur’an, rational custom makes their abandoning an easy decisive reply for harder hostility implausible.
rows.anchor: فكيف يجوز أن يقدروا على معارضته القريبة السهلة عليهم وذلك يدحض حجته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their eloquence and expertise, together with repeated public taunts about their incapacity, should have driven them to answer if able.
rows.anchor: وهم على ما هم عليه من الذرابة والسلاقة والمعرفة بوجوه الفصاحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated declarations of the Qur’an’s stature summon its opponents to hasten to a challenge, even where a passage is not itself a direct challenge.
rows.anchor: مما يدعوهم إلى المبادراة ويحضهم على المعارضة وإن لم يكن متحديا إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He includes the Qur’an’s description as guidance for the God-fearing among its declarations magnifying its status.
rows.anchor: هدى للمتقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arab poets competed in eloquence and oratory, holding familiar contests and boasting of their skill, which makes their failure to answer significant.
rows.anchor: وكانوا يتنافسون على الفصاحة والخطابة والذلاقة ويتبجحون بذلك ويتفاخرون بينهم

rows.speaker: علي بن أبى طالب
rows.claim: Ali’s eulogy uses the istirjaʿ at a great loss, then affirms acceptance of God’s decree and submission to His command.
rows.anchor: فإنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون رضينا عن الله قضاءه وسلمنا له أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The listeners remained silent until the speech ended, then wept so loudly that their voices rose.
rows.anchor: وسكت الناس حتى انقضى كلامه ثم بكوا حتى علت أصواتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects explaining the first generation’s inability only through reports of unseen events: that concedes the central claim that Qur’anic composition is inimitable.
rows.anchor: بأنهم لا يقدرون على معارضته في الإخبار عن الغيوب إن قدروا على مثل نظمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Later generations are even less able to match the Qur’an, since the first Arabs’ varied eloquence was unsurpassed and later speakers could at best equal it.
rows.anchor: فصاحة أولئك في وجوه ما كانوا يتفننون فيه من القول مما لا يزيد عليه فصاحة من بعدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same method establishes incapacity in every age: the challenge, human competitiveness, and obligation are constant; he cites the challenge to all humans and jinn.
rows.anchor: التحدي في الكل على جهة واحدة والتنافس في الطباع على حد واحد والتكليف على منهاج لا يختلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah, Gospel, and other scriptures are not inimitable in composition, though they may share the Qur’an’s inimitability in reporting unseen matters.
rows.anchor: ليس شيء من ذلك بمعجز في النظم والتأليف وإن كان معجزا كالقرآن فيما يتضمن من الإخبار عن الغيوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He argues other languages permit less eloquent differentiation: they have fewer names for one thing, less polysemy, and less scope for metaphor, allusion, and varied usage.
rows.anchor: لا نعرف فيها الكلمة الواحدة تتناول المعاني الكثيرة على ما تتناوله العربية وكذلك التصرف في الاستعارات والإشارات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s repeated description as clear Arabic, and its being kept from a foreign tongue, support the special eloquence of Arabic; intelligibility to its first hearers may also be a benefit.
rows.anchor: ويشهد لذلك من القرآن أن الله تعالى وصفه بأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims skilled in both Arabic and other languages recognize that the latter lack Arabic’s degrees of eloquence and stylistic distinction.
rows.anchor: قد عرفوا تلك الألسنة وهم من أهل البراعة فيها وفي العربية فقد وقفوا على أنه ليس فيها من التفاضل والفصاحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s unique inimitability is confirmed by the fact that neither scriptural communities nor Muslims claimed it for the Torah or Gospel.
rows.anchor: لم نجد أهل التوراة والإنجيل ادعوا الإعجاز لكتابهم ولا ادعى لهم المسلمون

rows.speaker: أفضل من رأيت من أهل العلم بالأدب
rows.claim: An eminent specialist says prose can accommodate greater eloquence than poetry because poetic form constrains speech and its development.
rows.anchor: أفضل من رأيت من أهل العلم بالأدب والحذق بهذه الصناعة مع تقدمه في الكلام يقول

rows.speaker: من يتقدم في صنعة الكلام
rows.claim: A skilled interlocutor counters that poetry may be more eloquent when it meets the conditions of eloquence and includes the causes of rhetorical beauty.
rows.anchor: وحضره من يتقدم في صنعة الكلام فراجعه في ذلك وذكر أنه لا يمتنع أن يكون الشعر أبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author sides with the poetry view: most Arab verbal brilliance is in poetry, while prose lacks comparable examples, despite the later refinement of letters.
rows.anchor: ويشهد عندي للقول الأخير أن معظم براعة كلام العرب في الشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although poetry narrows expression, it gathers and joins its parts; when fully polished in its genre, no human speech can rival it.
rows.anchor: وهو وإن ضيق نطاق القول فهو يجمع حواشيه ويضم أطرافه ونواحيه

rows.speaker: المتنبي
rows.claim: A report says al-Mutanabbi’s companion questioned his Qur’an reading; his reply that the eloquent Meccan was silenced would, if authentic, show his belief in poetry’s greater eloquence.
rows.anchor: عن المتنبي انه كان ينظر في المصحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To show the Qur’an’s superiority, he proposes examining an acclaimed, well-made poem for flaws, uneven structure, digressions, forced phrasing, and shifts between elevated and low diction.
rows.anchor: على مواضع خللها وعلى تفاوت نظمها وعلى اختلاف فصولها وعلى كثرة فضولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An accomplished critic recognizes each speaker’s style and ranks speech accurately, including whether a writer excels in only certain genres or throughout.
rows.anchor: فهو يميز قدر كل متكلم بكلامه وقدر كل كلام في نفسه ويحله محله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poets may excel selectively in praise, invective, humor, or description; an expert knows each person’s limits and can identify their later work.
rows.anchor: منهم من يجود في المدح دون الهجو ومنهم من يجود في الهجو وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Style recognition extends across poems, handwriting, letters, and sermons; confusion occurs when two writers briefly adopt similar methods.
rows.anchor: وكذلك أمر الخطب فإن اشتبه عليه البعض فهو لاشتباه الطريقين وتماثل الصورتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Experts distinguish Abu Tammam from al-Buhturi except where the former drops artifice and adopts an easy, bookish style resembling the latter.
rows.anchor: كما قد يشتبه شعر أبي تمام بشعر البحتري في القليل الذي يترك أبو تمام فيه التصنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distinct poetic textures of Abu Nuwas and Muslim, and Ibn al-Rumi and al-Buhturi, remain recognizable despite occasional overlap.
rows.anchor: سبك أبي نواس من سبك مسلم ولا نسج ابن الرومي من نسج البحتري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He lists recognizable styles among al-Aʿsha, Imruʾ al-Qays, al-Nabigha, Zuhayr, Jarir, al-Akhtal, al-Baʿith, and al-Farazdaq.
rows.anchor: وبين شعر امرئ القيس وبين شعر النابغة وزهير وبين شعر جرير والأخطل والبعيث والفرزدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The style of Abd al-Hamid’s generation differs from later letter writers; Ibn al-Amid blended earlier and later methods and developed a recognizable personal manner, despite slight occasional ambiguity.
rows.anchor: حتى إنه لا يشتبه عليه ما بين رسائل ابن العميد وبين رسائل أهل عصره ومن بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Punning can be learned from books such as Kitab al-Ajnas and Kitab al-ʿAyn, and antithesis is easier; the eloquence at issue in Qur’anic inimitability cannot be acquired by study.
rows.anchor: فأما الإطباق فهو أقرب منه وليس كذلك البيان والوجوه التي رأينا الإعجاز فيها لأنها لا تستوفي بالتعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Learnable capacities converge at a customary limit, like human strength; exceeding that limit breaks convention and can serve as a prophetic sign under the proper conditions.
rows.anchor: الذي يمكن أن يتوصل إليه بالتعلم يتقارب فيه الناس وتتناهى فيه العادات وهو كما يعلم من مقادير القوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exceptional lines or phrases may occur rarely in a poet’s or writer’s work, so a person may be famed for only one or two; if all speech sustained that level, it could be called miraculous.
rows.anchor: كالبيت البديع والقطعة الشريفة التي تتفق في ديوان شاعر والفقرة تتفق في رسالة كاتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans can produce a fine word or phrase, but cannot compose a surah or equivalent or attain the Qur’an’s level of eloquence and oratory.
rows.anchor: وإنما أنكرنا أن يقدروا على مثل نظم سورة أو نحوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic form may happen to appear in the Qur’an without giving the Qur’an the status of poetry.
rows.anchor: من أن صورة الشعر قد تتفق في القرآن وإن لم يكن له حكم الشعر

rows.speaker: ناس
rows.claim: Some hold that the miraculous measure is an entire surah or the longest verse.
rows.anchor: من الناس من قال مقدار كل سورة أو أطول آية فهو معجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He holds both proposed units—the surah and the longest verse—to be miraculous, because eloquence cannot be established in anything shorter.
rows.anchor: وعندنا كل واحد من الأمرين معجز والدلالة عليه ما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eloquence means conveying the self’s intended meaning with the best sense and strongest wording, reaching the utterance’s full purpose.
rows.anchor: الإبانة في الإبلاغ عن ذات النفس على أحسن معنى وأجزل لفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speech becomes miraculous when it surpasses eloquence’s customary limit and reaches a level even the most accomplished practitioners cannot attain.
rows.anchor: فإذا تجاوز حد البلاغة إلى حيث لا يقدر عليه أهل الصناعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an differs from other speech in its genre and style and in exceeding the human limit of eloquence.
rows.anchor: بجنسه وأسلوبه مباين لسائر كلامهم ثم بما يتضمن من تجاوزه في البلاغة الحد الذي يقدر عليه البشر

rows.speaker: السائل
rows.claim: An objection asks why a poet’s rare brilliant passage could not become the model for all his work through supreme mastery, just as the Qur’an might be exceptional speech.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل فإذا كان يجوز عندكم أن يتفق في شعر الشاعر قطعة عجيبة شاردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He answers that no poet or orator in the preserved record reached the proposed level: their poems, sermons, letters, and maxims are known, including those of Quss, Sahnun, Shaqq, and Satiḥ.
rows.anchor: لم نجد في شيء من ذلك ما يداني القرآن في البلاغة أو يشاكله في الإعجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After a long challenge and repeated rebukes, the Qur’an alone holds the lead; everyone failed, some recognizing their incapacity without understanding its cause.
rows.anchor: مع ما وقع من التحدي إليه الأمدة الطويلة وتقدم من التقريع في المجازاة الأمد المديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its rupture of customary human ability is a miracle and proof that the prophet who brought it is truthful in his claim and rightly guided.
rows.anchor: وخرق العادة إنما يقع بالمعجزات على وجه إقامة البرهان على النبوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hudaybiyya treaty set a ten-year truce, returned Quraysh escapees who lacked a guardian’s permission, left Muslim defectors with Quraysh, allowed either side to join either pact, and set the Prophet’s delayed three-day Meccan visit and travel arms.
rows.anchor: هذا ما صالح عليه محمد بن عبد الله سهيل ابن عمرو اصطلحا على وضع الحرب عن الناس عشر سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baqillani asks literate readers to compare Qur’anic eloquence with the Prophet’s recorded sermons and letters, which he says differ by a wide gulf.
rows.anchor: فما أحسب انه يشتبه عليك الفرق بين براعة القرآن وبين ما نسخناه لك من كلام الرسول الله في خطبه ورسائله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is not simply crafted prophetic rhetoric: sermons at major occasions and letters to kings receive serious effort, yet remain distinct from the Qur’an, which is divine in origin.
rows.anchor: فستعلم لا محالة أن نظم القرآن من الأمر الإلهي وأن كلام النبي من الأمر النبوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Companions’ and other eloquent speakers’ sermons share the Prophet’s human style; their differences are bounded variations among eloquent people, unlike the Qur’an’s distinction.
rows.anchor: وإنما يقع بين كلامه وكلام غيره ما يقع من التفاوت بين كلام الفصيحين وبين شعر الشاعرين

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says Arabs call one poetic line or a single pearl yatiim, two or three lines a nutfa, up to ten a qitʿa, and twenty a qasida.
rows.anchor: سمعت الفراء يقول العرب تسمي البيت الواحد يتيما وكذلك يقال الدرة اليتيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report derives qasida from accumulated marrow, as opposed to scattered marrow, and cites Labid’s stacked ostrich eggs as evidence for the sense of layered accumulation.
rows.anchor: ثم استشهد بقول لبيد ( فتذكر ثقلا رثيدا بعدما ألقت ذكاء يمينها في كافر )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rare, strange line, familiar proverb, or unusual meaning can occur spontaneously, even without deliberate effort to produce it.
rows.anchor: وكذلك يقع في الكلام البيت الوحشي والنادر والمثل السائر والمعنى الغريب

rows.speaker: بعض علماء هذه الصنعة
rows.claim: An unnamed master attributes such exceptional lines to deep command of the craft and broad knowledge, which can yield effects beyond calculation or classification.
rows.anchor: قال لي بعض علماء هذه الصنعة - وجاريته في ذلك - إن هذا مما لا سبب له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reaffirms that speech equal in measure to a surah is miraculous.
rows.anchor: فأما ما قلنا من أن ما بلغ قدر السورة معجز فإن ذلك صحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What resembles sajʿ in the Qur’an is not necessarily sajʿ: ordinary sajʿ makes wording follow the cadence, whereas Qur’anic phrasing follows the meaning.
rows.anchor: لأن السجع من الكلام يتبع المعنى فيه اللفظ الذي يؤدي السجع وليس كذلك ما اتفق مما هو في تقدير السجع من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When meaning is organized independently of cadence, the cadence is merely decorative rather than necessary to the meaning; he distinguishes this from meaning tied to sajʿ.
rows.anchor: ومتى انتظم المعنى بنفسه دون السجع كان مستجلبا لتحسين الكلام دون تصحيح المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if some passages combine the two patterns, a detailed treatment is outside the book’s scope; apparent non-sajʿ passages contain subtler benefits.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل فقد يتفق في القرآن ما يكون من القبيلين جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An occasional cadence used as a pause or ornament is not intentional enough to count as sajʿ, just as an isolated metrical line in prose is not poetry.
rows.anchor: لم يعد سجعا على ما قد بينا في القليل من الشعر كالبيت الواحد والمصراع والبيتين من الرجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Qur’an’s endings were sajʿ, their varying measures and methods would be defective, since sajʿ requires a regular pattern as poetry requires meter.
rows.anchor: لكان مذموما مرذولا لأن السجع إذا تفاوتت أوزانه واختلفت طرقه كان قبيحا من الكلام

rows.speaker: السائل
rows.claim: An objection asks whether the Prophet’s exceptional eloquence could have produced the Qur’an, since he is reported to have called himself the most eloquent Arab.
rows.anchor: إذا كان النبي أفصح العرب وقد قال هذا في حديث مشهور وهو صادق في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet did not challenge others to match his own speech; his difference from other eloquent people is an ordinary gradation like that between poets or orators.
rows.anchor: والقدر الذي بينه وبين كلام غيره من الفصحاء كقدر ما بين شعر الشاعرين وكلام الخطيبين في الفصاحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Comparing his sermons and prose letters with the Qur’an reveals a gulf like that between God’s speech and human speech; the Prophet’s words are not independently inimitable.
rows.anchor: إذا وازنا بين خطبه ورسائله وكلامه المنثور وبين نظم القرآن تبين من البون بينهما مثل ما بين كلام الله عز وجل وبين كلام الناس

rows.speaker: السائل
rows.claim: An objection invokes reports that Ibn Masʿud was uncertain whether the two protecting surahs or the qunut supplication belonged to the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: لم يشتبه على ابن مسعود الفصل بين المعوذتين وبين غيرهما من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls this an infidel’s confusion: the Companions knew the Qur’an and its surah count, and no Qur’anic material could have been unknown to them.
rows.anchor: لأن عندنا أن الصحابة لم يخف عليهم ما هو من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If material was absent from Ibn Masʿud’s codex, he may have relied on communal memorization rather than denied its Qur’anic status; the reports are solitary and insufficient for such a claim.
rows.anchor: وقد يجوز أن يكون شذ عن مصحفه لا لأنه نفاه من القرآن بل عول على حفظ الكل إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud may have written the qunut supplication on the back of his codex as a personal reminder, as people write prayers on their own copies.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكتب على ظهر مصحفه دعاء القنوت لئلا ينساه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports of codex differences do not prove denial: a memorizer might err or forget a few letters, but the author rejects a broader claim against Ibn Masʿud.
rows.anchor: ونحن لا ننكر أن يغلط في حروف معدودة كما يغلط الحافظ في حروف وينسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had Ibn Masʿud rejected the two surahs, the Companions would have debated and publicized so grave a dispute; their agreement on the codex cannot be undone by isolated fabricated reports.
rows.anchor: فقد تناظروا في أقل من هذا وهذا أمر يوجب التكفير والتضليل
